content_voiceover: This diagram illustrates the spectrum of genetic and non-genetic factors that shift inhibitor risk up or down, arranged along a reduce to increase gradient. Genetic, non-modifiable factors include F8 genotype, where missense mutations carry the lowest risk, progressing through small insertions or deletions, splice site mutations, inversions, nonsense mutations, up to large deletions which carry the highest risk. Inhibitor family history also matters, a negative family history lowers risk, while a positive history, especially in siblings rather than more distant relatives, raises it substantially. Ethnicity plays a role too, with Caucasian patients at lower risk than non-Caucasian patients. Immunogenotype variants also modulate risk, CTLA-4 tends to be protective, while TNF-alpha and IL-10 polymorphisms increase risk. Below the dashed line are non-genetic, modifiable factors, chiefly treatment approach, regular prophylaxis reduces inhibitor risk, whereas intensive treatment, high-dose factor, and surgery increase it. This framework is useful for understanding why some patients are inherently higher risk while others' risk can be actively managed through treatment choices.
keypoints: F8 genotype risk ranges from missense mutations, lowest, to large deletions, highest
Positive inhibitor family history, especially in siblings, raises risk
Non-Caucasian ethnicity and TNF-alpha or IL-10 variants increase risk; CTLA-4 is protective
Regular prophylaxis lowers risk while intensive or high-dose treatment and surgery raise it
keypoint_voiceover: Key points to hold onto. F8 genotype risk climbs from missense mutations up to large deletions, which carry the highest inhibitor risk. A positive family history, particularly in siblings, raises risk substantially. Non-Caucasian ethnicity and certain immune genotype variants like TNF-alpha and IL-10 increase risk, while CTLA-4 tends to be protective. And on the modifiable side, regular prophylaxis lowers inhibitor risk, while intensive treatment, high dose factor, and surgery raise it.
